title: Check yourself: The computer use tool: the toolset, the loop and the scale

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team adds the computer use toolset to a request and expects Claude to press keys on the machine. Which part performs the keystroke?

options.text: Claude itself, through a remote link the toolset opens
options.says: Ruled out because the documentation describes the loop as one where the application translates the calls, and Claude "never touches the machine" in this design.

options.text: An Anthropic server that replays the call on the desktop
options.says: Ruled out because "Your application receives the tool use requests, translates them into actions in your computing environment", and no Anthropic server replays them.

options.text: The beta header on the request, which enables key presses
options.says: Ruled out because "The request needs no beta header."

options.text: Your own program, in an environment it controls
options.says: The page says the toolset "gives Claude 17 member tools such as screenshot, left_click, type, and zoom, and your application runs every call in an environment you control."

questions.stem: A single reply from Claude contains a click, a text entry and a screenshot request, and the click fails. What should the application send back for the last two calls?

options.text: Error results with the fixed halt wording, and neither action run
options.says: The page says "if one fails, don't run the rest", and that every later action gets `is_error: true` with exactly the text `Not executed: an earlier computer action in this turn failed.`

options.text: The screenshot for the last call and an error for the text entry
options.says: Ruled out because a screenshot after a failed click would run against a screen that no longer looks as expected, and "if one fails, don't run the rest".

options.text: Nothing for them, since the batch is abandoned after a failure
options.says: Ruled out because leaving a block unanswered is an invalid request, "so an agent loop that reads only the first block fails on its next call".

options.text: Normal results for both, because the earlier failure does not matter
options.says: Ruled out because "Later actions depend on earlier ones, because the type enters text into whatever the click focused."

questions.stem: The application shrinks every screenshot to half its size before returning it. Claude replies with a click at a spot in the shrunken image. What must the application do before clicking?

options.text: Click exactly where Claude said, since the toolset converts coordinates
options.says: Ruled out because "coordinates are always in the pixel space of the screenshots you return", which is the shrunken picture here.

options.text: Treat the numbers as relative to the last zoomed region
options.says: Ruled out because after a zoom Claude "still expresses coordinates in the full screenshot's space, never relative to the zoomed image".

options.text: Scale the position back up by the factor it used, onto the real display
options.says: The page quotes the documentation: "If you scale screenshots down before returning them, scale Claude's coordinates back up before applying them to the real display."

options.text: Give the toolset the true display size so that the API scales for you
options.says: Ruled out because "the toolset takes no display dimensions and the API doesn't downscale for you".

origin.section: Screenshots must fit, and coordinates are theirs
